q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of areca leaf plates?
title: Areca leaf plate carbon footprint
short: Read the unit's electricity for heated presses, washing and drying, multiply by the grid factor and divide by plates passed. Add collection transport and packing. The leaf is a crop residue, so the press electricity is usually most of the figure.
audience: Areca leaf plate makers in Karnataka and Kerala

ul: Fallen areca sheaths, collected and stored; record the diesel used to collect them.
Washing and sun or dryer drying.
Hydraulic or pneumatic presses with heated dies, the main electricity load.

p: Report per plate by size. Rejected plates and trimmings are usually composted, not counted as product.

example.title: Worked example: leaf plate unit per plate (one month)
lines: Collection diesel: 300 litres x 2.68 = 804 kg CO2
Plant total: 5,064 / 200,000 = 0.0253 kg CO2 per plate
Add packaging for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
